project.name: hostap
project.commit_note: Sample metadata leaves `vulnerable_commit` empty. The exact staged vulnerable source traced here is the prepared checkout at `81121319a9e5cfcd4531fda7ce869b113d79caa0`, whose line map matches the staged `patch.diff` and the saved `wpabuf_free -> p2p_device_free -> p2p_flush` sanitizer stack.

classification.classification_note: The saved AddressSanitizer symptom is a later `SEGV` / wild-addr READ in `wpabuf_free`, but the patched source-level bug is the preceding 152-byte write into the 128-byte heap-resident `dev->info.wps_sec_dev_type_list` array.

bug_description.original: The parsing and copying of the WPS secondary device types list in P2P group client fails to validate the length of the contents when handling P2P group information, which encodes this data in a different attribute. This lack of validation can result in writing beyond the allocated memory area for these entries, leading to memory corruption within an instance of struct p2p_device. This may cause invalid operations and unexpected behavior when freeing pointers from the corrupted memory.
bug_description.normalized: The staged 232-byte witness is a single vendor-specific P2P IE (`dd e6 50 6f 9a 09 ...`) whose attributes are a 6-byte Device ID `20:20:20:20:20:20` and a 214-byte Group Info block. `p2p_parse_attribute()` aliases that Group Info span, and `p2p_group_info_parse()` admits its only client descriptor by reading the descriptor-length byte `0xd5` (213), checking that it fits inside the 214-byte Group Info attribute, and setting `cend = g + 213`. Within that bounded descriptor, the parser later reads `num_sec_dev_types = 0x13` (19) and still passes the present source-length guard because the descriptor also carries the required 152 secondary-device-type bytes. `p2p_add_group_clients()` therefore creates a fresh zeroed `struct p2p_device` for client address `20:20:20:20:20:ff`, and vulnerable `p2p_copy_client_info()` computes `wps_sec_dev_type_list_len = 8 * 19 = 152` before copying all 152 bytes into the fixed 128-byte `wps_sec_dev_type_list` array. In that 152-byte source span, bytes 79 and 110 are `0xff`, but the final 24 bytes that spill past the destination are all `0x20`; on the staged x86_64 build, that 24-byte overwrite clobbers the following `wps_sec_dev_type_list_len` field and the first two `wps_vendor_ext` pointers with `0x2020202020202020`. At fuzzer teardown, `p2p_flush()` frees that corrupted device, `p2p_device_free()` passes the forged `wps_vendor_ext` pointer into `wpabuf_free()`, and `wpabuf_free()` crashes when it tries to read `buf->flags`, matching the saved AddressSanitizer `SEGV` / wild-addr-read.

source.description: First project parser statement that materializes the attacker-controlled Group Info attribute as a `(pointer,length)` pair later consumed by the vulnerable client-info copy path.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is exactly 232 bytes. Parsed as a vendor-specific P2P IE, it begins `dd e6 50 6f 9a 09`; within that IE, attribute id 14 (`P2P_ATTR_GROUP_INFO`) has `len = 214` and contains one 213-byte client descriptor. `p2p_parse_p2p_ie()` passes that attribute's `data` and `len` into `p2p_parse_attribute()`, which aliases them here.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: Actual crash site. `buf` is a forged high address loaded from the overflow-corrupted `dev->info.wps_vendor_ext[0]` slot, so reading `buf->flags` dereferences attacker-derived non-heap memory.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `AddressSanitizer: SEGV` / `wild-addr-read` at `wpabuf_free /src/hostap/src/utils/wpabuf.c:201:11` with stack `wpabuf_free -> p2p_device_free -> p2p_flush`.

root_cause.description: The copy uses the attacker-derived 152-byte length against a fixed 128-byte destination without the patch's missing `> WPS_SEC_DEV_TYPE_MAX_LEN` clamp, so it overwrites adjacent fields inside the heap-allocated `struct p2p_device`.
root_cause.note: The staged patch inserts `if (dev->info.wps_sec_dev_type_list_len > WPS_SEC_DEV_TYPE_MAX_LEN) dev->info.wps_sec_dev_type_list_len = WPS_SEC_DEV_TYPE_MAX_LEN;` immediately before this copy, which would reduce the witnessed 152-byte copy to 128 bytes and leave the following pointer fields intact.

tainted_value_origin.description: This is where the vulnerable path stores the witness's `Number of Secondary Device Types` byte `0x13` as semantic parser state and aliases the following 152 attacker-controlled secondary-device-type bytes for the later copy.

parser_admitted.description: After `p2p_parse_ies()` accepts the staged P2P IE and populates both `msg.device_id` and `msg.group_info`, the scan-result path enters the vulnerable Group Info client-copy logic on this call.

fine_trace.note: Source. The staged vendor-specific P2P IE contains attribute id 14 (`P2P_ATTR_GROUP_INFO`) with `len = 214`, and this statement records that exact byte span for later group-client parsing.

The first byte of the only Group Info entry is the client-descriptor length `0xd5` (213). This check admits that descriptor inside the 214-byte Group Info attribute and records `cend` as the end of that specific descriptor, which later bounds the secondary-device-type list.

Within the descriptor bounded by step 2, the parser consumes the fixed fields up to the `Number of Secondary Device Types` byte. The first 6 bytes become `cli->p2p_device_addr = 20:20:20:20:20:ff`, distinct from the outer scan-result Device ID `20:20:20:20:20:20`, so the later group-client path targets a separate client `p2p_device`.
At the secondary-device-type count byte, the parser reads `0x13`, so `len = 19`, and advances `g` to the first 8-byte secondary-device-type entry.

fine_trace.code:
if (8 * len > cend - g)
	return -1; /* invalid data */
fine_trace.note: Present source-length guard. Step 2 set `cend` at the end of the 213-byte descriptor, and step 4 left `g` at the first secondary-device-type byte, so `cend - g = 189` for the staged witness. With `8 * 19 = 152`, this predicate is false and the parser accepts the source list. It only checks that the descriptor contains 152 source bytes, not that the later destination has room for 152 bytes.

Tainted value origin. The accepted count `19` is stored in `cli->num_sec_dev_types`, and `cli->sec_dev_types` aliases the following 152 attacker-controlled bytes. In the staged witness, the 79th and 110th bytes of that span are `0xff` and the other 150 bytes are `0x20`; critically, the final 24 bytes that later overflow past the destination are all `0x20`.

Reached from `p2p_add_group_clients` for the parsed client address from step 3. Because the only peer already present is the outer GO entry at `20:20:20:20:20:20`, this call allocates a fresh zeroed client `struct p2p_device`, links it into `p2p->devices`, and leaves `dev->info.wps_vendor_ext[0..9] == NULL` before the vulnerable copy runs.

This derives the copy length `152` from the tainted count `19`. The destination `dev->info.wps_sec_dev_type_list` is only 128 bytes (`WPS_SEC_DEV_TYPE_MAX_LEN`) inside the heap object from step 7, followed by the 8-byte `wps_sec_dev_type_list_len` field and the `wps_vendor_ext[10]` pointer array. The vulnerable code applies no `> WPS_SEC_DEV_TYPE_MAX_LEN` clamp here; the patch adds that missing guard immediately before the copy.

Root cause. This copies all 152 secondary-device-type bytes from step 6 into the 128-byte destination, overflowing by 24 bytes. Although the full 152-byte source span is not uniform, its last 24 bytes (`cli->sec_dev_types[128..151]`) are all `0x20`, so on the staged x86_64 build they overwrite the 8-byte `wps_sec_dev_type_list_len` field and the first two 8-byte `wps_vendor_ext` pointers, changing both pointers from NULL to `0x2020202020202020`.

At fuzzer teardown `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` calls `p2p_deinit`, which always calls `p2p_flush`. Because step 7 linked the corrupted client object into `p2p->devices`, this cleanup loop reaches that same overwritten `dev` and hands it to `p2p_device_free`.
The loop begins at `i = 0`. Step 9 already changed `dev->info.wps_vendor_ext[0]` and `[1]` to `0x2020202020202020`, so this first iteration passes a non-NULL forged high address into `wpabuf_free`.

Sink. The `buf == NULL` early return is bypassed because step 11 supplied the non-zero forged pointer `0x2020202020202020`. Reading `buf->flags` through that high address triggers the saved AddressSanitizer `SEGV` / `wild-addr-read` at `wpabuf.c:201`, with stack `wpabuf_free -> p2p_device_free -> p2p_flush`.

allocation_context.note: The overflowed `wps_sec_dev_type_list` destination and the later-corrupted `wps_vendor_ext[]` pointer slots are fields inside the heap-allocated `struct p2p_device` created here.

free_context.note: The corrupted pointer is first consumed from `dev->info.wps_vendor_ext[0]` here during teardown.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch clamps `dev->info.wps_sec_dev_type_list_len` to `WPS_SEC_DEV_TYPE_MAX_LEN` before the `os_memcpy`, so the witnessed 152-byte copy becomes 128 bytes and the adjacent `wps_vendor_ext` pointers are no longer corrupted. Stage 02 did not execute the fixed image.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: Yes. The overflowed destination and the later-corrupted `wps_vendor_ext[]` slots are fields inside the `struct p2p_device` allocated at `p2p_create_device:436`, and that same object is later traversed by `p2p_flush` and freed on the crashing stack.

format.name: staged vendor-specific P2P IE carrying one oversized Group Info client descriptor
format.contract: The verified witness is the exact 232-byte staged `poc`. Parsed as a P2P vendor IE (`dd e6 50 6f 9a 09`), it contains a Device ID attribute `20:20:20:20:20:20` and a Group Info attribute of length 214 whose only client-descriptor length byte is `0xd5` and whose `Number of Secondary Device Types` byte is `0x13`. Within that descriptor's 152-byte secondary-device-type span, bytes 79 and 110 are `0xff` and the other bytes are `0x20`, so the final 24 copied bytes that run past the 128-byte `wps_sec_dev_type_list` destination are all `0x20`. Those exact bytes make `p2p_group_info_parse()` admit the descriptor, make `p2p_copy_client_info()` derive `8 * 19 = 152`, overflow the destination by 24 bytes, and corrupt `wps_vendor_ext[0]` / `[1]` to `0x2020202020202020` before teardown.
